newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Qualceram announces placing to raise 6.2 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: Qualceram announces placing to raise 6.2 mln stg.

text.p: Qualceram Plc, an Irish manufacturer of bathroom suites, said on Friday that it had successfully placed 4,309,483 ordinary shares at 143 pence sterling with institutions in London, Edinburgh, Glasgow and Dublin.
The placing, which values Qualceram at 20 million sterling, will raise 6.2 million sterling gross in total including 1.8 million of new money, the company said in a statement.
It was done by English Trust Limited through Davy Stockbrokers and Teather & Greenwood.

The new money raised will be directed into three planned capital expenditure projects. The projects involve increasing the manufacturing capacity of ceramic products, developing the acrylic baths plant and opening a distribution depot in Dublin.
Qualceram, which is seeking a full listing on both the London and Irish Stock Exchanges, said its founder shareholders would hold 64 percent of its share capital after the flotation.

"The flotation will allow Qualceram to fulfil its short-term plans for expansion and benefit to a greater extent from the excellent opportunities available to us in a growing market," John O'Loughlin, managing and finance director of Qualceram, said.
Qualceram, which was formed in 1988, said its turnover had increased by 49 percent in the last three years while pre-tax profit was up 76 percent.
It reported a pre-tax profit of 1.54 million Irish pounds on turnover of 7.33 million last year and the company said trading performance in the year to date was ahead of last year.

"Qualceram will benefit from new distribution centres now operational in Yorkshire and France, new product development and recent requests to supply nearly 3,000 suites to new houses and hotels in Ireland," it said.
Dealings in the company's shares are expected to commence on April 24, 1997.
